question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
method: best-api-review/history-v3; third-failed-fix recovery; redesign-from-first-principles hard-cut comparison
trigger: TaskHub #46 reporter contradiction against pushed commit ae7f2a83c8: keeping a collapsed native caret in selection-controller import/export still leaves the real editor unfocused because the root pointer-drag ownership transition independently clears every browser Selection range.
requirements: When a browser-owned drag becomes a projected selection, the existing Editable must retain browser keyboard focus and one collapsed writable native caret throughout the ownership handoff.
The handoff must not call removeAllRanges for an expanded projected selection; the existing DOM selection export is the sole owner of the native caret representation.
Inactive-selection paint is a direct failure oracle for this release path, while floating-toolbar visibility is never evidence of focus or keyboard ownership.
Ordinary model selections may retain their existing DOM clear/export behavior, and a genuine external focus transfer must still win.
Retained-fragment identity, projected paint and projected commands remain private mounted-view responsibilities without a new public API or copied-UI repair.
evidenceReuse: Retains the prior exact-Editable, projected-selection and collapsed-native-caret ownership decisions. Rechecks the actual root mousemove/mouseup path after the reporter contradiction and finds a second removeAllRanges call in applyProjectedDragSelectionFromEvent that bypasses selection-controller entirely. The prior native-caret contracts therefore proved only export behavior, not the browser-to-projected drag handoff that still destroyed focus.
summary: Pursue one ownership handoff: when root interaction converts a native drag to a projected view selection, call the existing DOM selection export with preserveScroll so it installs the projected collapsed caret. Keep removeAllRanges only for the non-projected fallback, and keep toolbar and inactive-selection consumers out of the repair.

reconciliation.question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
reconciliation.reason: The expanded projected selection still needs one collapsed native caret owned by the exact Editable, and toolbar visibility remains only a downstream consumer.

reconciliation.question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
reconciliation.reason: The prior repair incorrectly treated selection-controller as the only native range clearer and left the root projected-drag handoff calling removeAllRanges.

alternatives: Delete projected selection and flatten retained content into the model range: rejected because retained fragment identity and multi-segment command targeting are independent current jobs.
Focus the Editable on mouseup or in a timer: rejected because it repairs after ownership was already destroyed and can steal a genuine external focus transfer.
Close the floating toolbar or clear inactivity paint when focus is missing: rejected because it hides the visible symptoms while the keyboard target remains broken.
Keep the root removeAllRanges call and add another collapsed caret afterward: rejected because it preserves the destructive intermediate state and duplicates the existing DOM selection export owner.

Route the projected root-drag handoff through syncDOMSelectionToEditor with preserveScroll: chosen because the selection controller already resolves the exact writable projected caret and the interaction still owns the native drag at that synchronous boundary.
proofLimits: This review identifies the previously unmodified removeAllRanges call and selects the private handoff owner. Focused unit contracts can prove that the projected branch delegates to DOM export without clearing the browser range and that export collapses to one caret. Per the user's instruction, real browser focus, inactivity paint and first-key behavior remain unverified and delegated to the user.
